```{r setup, include=FALSE}

ggplot2::theme_set(suzR::theme_suzR())

library(tidyverse)

alignments <- read_tsv('../data/alignments.csv')
episodes <- read_tsv('../data/episodes.csv')

```

### The mystery

I recently stumbled across an old John Oliver episode from Season 1. The pace of the episode was so noticeably slower as if I had YouTube on half speed. My interest was piqued: has John Oliver become more fast-paced over time?

That's a rather straightforward corpus linguistic task: we can measure speech rate in words per minute or syllables per second, and look at the average duration of pauses - metrics which will probably approximate John's speech style space over time.

### The data

From a [list of main segments of Last Week Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Last_Week_Tonight_with_John_Oliver_episodes) and their YouTube links, I fetched the audio, auto-generated subtitles, and some meta data such as file duration and views (using [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp)). [Gentle](https://github.com/lowerquality/gentle) aligns the audio to the subtitles and determine the beginning and end of each word. Gentle was the only forced-aligner I could find that works reasonably reliably on files larger than a few seconds - while this comes at the cost of accuracy, given the amount of data for the question to be answered, it's a workable trade-off.

Two issues: First, John Oliver frequently features clips with speech from other people, which would have to be removed. To assess, I manually filtered other people's text from the files for 20 episodes, and, if anything, the reported effects would be more pronounced, hence I decided using all data is good enough for the current purpose, and treat other people's speech as noise - as lots of data tends to make such problems be much less influential. Second, 

```{r inspect}
alignments |> 
  filter(ytid == '_-0J49_9lwc') |> 
  head(8) |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Forced-alignment for one file")
```
```{r}
# For wpm on episodes:
episodes <- episodes |> 
  mutate(viewers_m = viewers * 1000000,
         wpm = wrds/length * 60,
         spm = syls/length,
         vlr = likes/views,
         vcr = comms/views)

## TV viewers per episode
episodes |> 
  filter(!is.na(viewers_m)) |> 
  select(ytdate, ep_id, season, viewers_m) |> 
  ggplot(aes(ytdate, viewers_m)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = season)) +
  #geom_line(group = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'loess') +
  labs(title = 'Last Week Tonight: Popularity',
       subtitle = 'TV viewer rise and decline',
       x = 'Year',
       y = 'TV viewers (millions)') +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = '1 year', date_labels = "%Y") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1))

```
